question: A regular right pyramid has a square base with a side length of 12 cm. Its slant height is 10 cm. What is its volume?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a regular square pyramid, Vertical Height (h) = √(l² − (a/2)²).

⇒ h = √(10² − 6²) = √(100 − 36) = √64 = 8 cm.

Volume = 1/3 × Base Area × h

⇒ Volume = 1/3 × (12 × 12) × 8 = 48 × 8 = 384 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 384 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Base side = 12 cm
 l = 10 cm
 h = ?
 6 cm

**Given:**

⇒ Side of the square base (a) = 12 cm

⇒ Slant height (l) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Volume of a right pyramid = 1/3 × Base Area × Vertical Height

⇒ Vertical Height (h) = √(l² − r²) where r is half of the base side length.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Base Area = a × a = 12 × 12 = 144 cm²

⇒ Half of the base side length (r) = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm

⇒ Applying Pythagoras theorem to find the vertical height:

⇒ h² + r² = l²

⇒ h² + 6² = 10²

⇒ h² + 36 = 100

⇒ h² = 64

⇒ h = 8 cm

⇒ Volume = 1/3 × 144 × 8

⇒ Volume = 48 × 8 = 384 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 384 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Lateral Surface Area of Pyramid

It is the total area of all the triangular lateral faces. Formula: LSA = 1/2 × Perimeter of Base × Slant Height.

Total Surface Area of Pyramid

It comprises both the lateral faces and the base. Formula: TSA = Lateral Surface Area + Base Area.

Slant Height vs Vertical Height

Vertical height is the perpendicular distance from the apex straight down to the center of the base, whereas slant height is measured along the lateral face from the apex to the midpoint of the base edge.
